C0.quote: We study diversity in approval-based committee elections

C1.quote: requires Ω(m2 ) non-adaptive queries, where m is the number of candidates
C1.note: Query-complexity bounds and approximation algorithms (AL) dominate. The experiments compare greedy and local search against approval voting on Max Cover (CC) score, which is a rule-performance-against-objective result (WD). Experiments use Polis data (EM) and synthetic data (SI).

C2.1.value: approval profile; approval sets; approval ballots; votes; query responses

C2.2.quote: every voter vi ∈ V approves of a subset of the candidates

C2.3.quote: the voters are inaccurate in reporting their true approvals
C2.3.note: The introduction also refers to voters' true beliefs and opinions.

C2.4.quote: a p-inaccurate query as Ap (i, j) := A(i, j) ⊕ X
C2.4.note: True approvals A and reported answers Ap have separate notation in the inaccurate setting.

C3.1.quote: we assume each query A(i, j) is incorrect with a probability p
C3.1.note: Deviations are random noise, not strategic choices.

C3.2.quote: for accurate information, we write A(i, j) to query the opinion
C3.2.note: In the accurate settings a query is said to return the voter's opinion, i.e. their true approval, in contrast to inaccurate reporting.

C3.3.note: No reason is given for accurate answers.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notion is used for voters in the model. 'Unsatisfiable' appears only once, in preprocessing.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.note: Chamberlin-Courant score measures representation of voters.

C5.2.quote: voters are inaccurate in reporting their true approvals
C5.2.note: The CC score is computed on the true approvals A, which are notationally separate from the noisy reports Ap.

C1.reason: The experiments evaluate rules against the Chamberlin-Courant representation objective, comparing them with approval voting, so WD applies to a main result.

C3.2.reason: The paper says in words that accurate queries return the voter's opinion, as opposed to inaccurately reporting their true approvals.

C3.3.reason: Since C3.2 is STATED and no justification for accurate reporting is offered, NONE applies.

C5.2.reason: The objective is defined on the true approval profile A, which the paper distinguishes from the submitted responses Ap.

C6.VOT.reason: The voters' response behaviour, accurate or randomly corrupted, is stated in words as an assumption.
